This developer series explains **why calls occur**, not just which names appear
in source. Read articles in numeric order. Internal functions are implementation
seams, not a supported public R API. The app remains a single-analyst local preview;
it does not yet run L1 analysis or connect to Enterprise.

## Entry and ownership

| Call or registration | Responsibility | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `run_app()` → `fgstudio_app()` | Bind the Shiny app to loopback | `R/app.R` |
| `fgstudio_app()` → `local_study_store()` | Construct a server-owned storage adapter | `R/study_store.R` |
| `fgstudio_app()` → `mod_study_ui()` | Build the workspace form | `R/mod_study.R` |
| Shiny session callback → `mod_study_server()` | Create session-local reactive state | `R/mod_study.R` |
| Current-revision observer → `mod_boundary_server()` and `mod_streams_server()` | Create isolated editors for the opened revision | `R/mod_study.R` |

An arrow describes a call or explicitly identified callback. Shiny observers are
registered during setup and run later in response to invalidation; this is not
a single synchronous sequence. Merely constructing the app can create its data
directory, so this article does not launch it during package builds.

```{r public-interface}
sort(getNamespaceExports("fgstudio"))
```

The public entry points are `fgstudio_app` and `run_app`. The storage object is a
list of closures created by `local_study_store`; a call such as `store$create()`
cannot be understood by looking only for a top-level function named `create`.

## Create, reopen, revise

| Action | App/adapter route | Backend and result |
|---|---|---|
| Create Study Area | create observer → `store$create` | `fluvgeo::start_study_context`; reread persisted context |
| Open study | open observer → `store$read` | `fluvgeo::read_study_context`; highest numbered local revision |
| Reload saved study | one-time URL observer → `restore_study` → `store$read` | Same validated read path; no new revision |
| Edit Study Area name/Purpose | modal save → `store$rename` / `store$set_purpose` → local `revise` | `fluvgeo::revise_study_context`; new immutable revision |
| Save drawn boundary | `mod_boundary_server` → `store$save_boundary` | Containment check, then context revision |
| Rename Stream/Reach | `study_feature_names` → `store$rename_feature` → local `revise` | `fluvgeo::rename_study_feature`; identity and geometry retained |

`revise` accepts a **function-valued writer**. Its default is
`fluvgeo::revise_study_context`, but Stream and Reach operations inject other
writers. It checks the expected source path, chooses a new destination, invokes
`writer(source, destination, ...)`, then rereads the result. Treating every call
to `revise` as the default backend function would misrepresent this architecture.

The opaque folder key is not the Study Area UUID. Both are server-generated.
Files named `study.gpkg` and `revision-000001.gpkg` are context snapshots; companion
GeoPackages carry source evidence. Back up the entire study folder. Publication
is not a multi-file transaction, and an error can leave unreferenced evidence.

## Editor lifetime and unsaved work

Successful saves call `on_saved`, update `current`, destroy old observers and
construct a new revision-specific editor. Inactive editors cannot save. Same-study
revisions can retain selected draft inputs, but previews must be recomputed.
Explicit reopen clears transient work even if the revision has not changed.
Workspace New protects unfinished work with a discard confirmation; it does not
delete saved studies.

Create/Open place the opaque key in the current tab's `study` query parameter
using Shiny's replace-history update. A new session reads it once, after initial
inputs, through the normal validated store; no global last-opened study is shared
between sessions. Other query parameters are retained. Invalid or missing-on-disk
keys produce the normal open error, not a guessed fallback. Workspace New clears
the key. This is a local resume link, not portable data or access control.

Reload restores only the latest persisted revision, not navigation tabs, drafts,
validation results or previews. Both CRS forms show saved definitions and status;
their local messages distinguish failed validation from a completed save. Test
`test-study-reload.R` uses a fresh storage adapter and session against saved files.

Boundary saves reject exclusion of existing child areas; they do not automatically
move children. Name/Purpose saves do not authorize scientific or geometry changes.
Stream/Reach rename lists display names for selection but submit stable IDs.

## Where to investigate a failure

| Symptom | First source | Focused tests |
|---|---|---|
| Wrong study/revision after save | `R/mod_study.R`, `R/study_store.R` | `test-study-module.R`, `test-study-store.R` |
| Unsaved work lost on task change | `R/mod_boundary.R` | `test-task-navigation.R` |
| Name save or sorting wrong | `R/study_feature_names.R`, `R/saved_feature_display.R` | `test-feature-names.R`, `test-saved-feature-display.R` |
| Boundary publication rejected | `store$check_boundary` and fluvgeo containment | `test-boundary.R` |

Test files live under `tests/testthat`. Never start the analyst preview in an R
process that ran mocked tests. Use `dev/scripts/run-dev.ps1` for a fresh process.
